text:
Maya: Heads up — opened a quick PR to clarify how function-calling schema validators should handle optional fields. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512

Joel: Thanks, will take a look. What's the migration impact? Are we changing validator behaviour?

Maya: Not changing runtime. Just docs + SDK examples. Adding an explicit example for the response envelope vs bare JSON and a short migration note for teams doing strict schema checks.

Sam: Can you paste the JS snippet here? I want to ensure parity with Python and the SDK helpers.

Maya: Sure:
```js
// recommended parse example for JS SDK
const resp = await client.responses.create({
  model: 'redwood-open-1',
  input: prompt,
  parse: {
    type: 'json_schema',
    schema: responseSchema,
  },
});
const data = resp.output?.[0]?.content;
```

Maya: Also added a short note about guardrails: prefer schema-first validation and a fallback to raw string parse when the model returns unexpected types. See PR description for the rationale.

Joel: Looks good. Small suggestion: add a one-liner about streaming — "streamed tokens may require incremental parsing / buffering". Sam, can you add the Python streaming parse snippet?

Sam: Yep, will add a minimal Python example showing incremental assembly + json.loads. Will submit a follow-up commit today.

Lisa: FYI, analytics wants a link to the evals notebook that will track parse regressions. Can we add that under "Migration notes"?

Maya: Done — added the link and a checklist item to run the notebook after rolling docs changes. Also fixed a broken internal link on the Function calling page while I was in there.

docs-bot: Docs site build for PR 512 — passed :white_check_mark:

Joel: Reviewed & approved. Maya — feel free to merge after Sam's snippet or we can merge now and patch later.

Maya: I'll wait for Sam's snippet so examples are symmetric. Thanks all! :tada:
